summary: 杭州临安人；开平元年梁封吴越王，据两浙；筑捍海塘，治钱塘江堤，保杭嘉；对中原称臣纳贡，保境安民；长兴三年卒。
summary_en: A man of Lin'an in Hangzhou; in the 1st year of Kaiping Liang made him King of Wuyue, holding the two Zhe; he built the sea wall, diking the Qiantang to protect Hang and Jia; a vassal paying tribute to the Central Plains, he kept his borders and his people. He died in the 3rd year of Changxing.

bio_md:
# 吴越太祖 · 主要事迹

钱镠，杭州临安人。开平元年（907），后梁封钱镠为吴越王，据两浙——吴越国之始。钱镠出身盐贩，「起自寒微」，而治两浙数十年，政绩卓著：筑钱塘江捍海塘，「以石为堤，以御潮患」，杭州遂成东南都会；又广建城郭、兴修水利、劝课农桑，「满城桃李，夹道花木」。

钱镠之政，以「事大保境」为纲：对中原五代政权，一律称臣纳贡，不称帝、不争霸——「钱氏之祚，赖事大以延」。吴越以两浙弹丸之地，在五代纷争中保境安民八十余年，百姓「安居乐业」，为十国中政局最稳者。

长兴三年，钱镠卒，年八十一。史评钱镠：「有功于浙，民到于今称之。」吴越虽偏安一隅，然钱镠之筑塘、治杭、保境，为杭州成为「人间天堂」奠定根基；钱氏后裔于太平兴国三年纳土归宋，「以善终」，亦为乱世中难得之结局。

> 参考：点校本《新五代史》卷067《吴越世家》。

bio_parts_en.value:
Qian Liu, a man of Lin'an in Hangzhou, was made King of Wuyue by Later Liang in the 1st year of Kaiping (907), holding the two Zhe — the beginning of Wuyue. A salt-dealer who "rose from the meanest," he governed the two Zhe for decades with real achievement: he built the Qiantang sea wall, "stone for the dike to hold the tide," and Hangzhou became the great city of the southeast; he raised walls, mended the waterways, and urged farming — "the streets full of peach and plum, the ways lined with flowers."

His rule ran on "serving the great and keeping the borders": to every dynasty of the Central Plains he was a vassal, never emperor, never contending — "the fortunes of the Qian were prolonged by serving the great." On the sliver of the two Zhe, amid the wars of the Five Dynasties, Wuyue kept its borders and its people for over eighty years, the most stable state of the Ten.

He died in the 3rd year of Changxing, aged eighty-one. The histories say: "he served Zhe well; the people praise him to this day." Wuyue hugged one corner, but Qian Liu's wall, his Hangzhou, and his peace laid the base of the "earthly paradise" of Hangzhou; and his heirs, surrendering their lands to Song in the 3rd year of Taiping Xingguo, ended well — a rare ending in that age.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Xin Wudaishi*, ch. 67 ("Annals of Wuyue").
